title_en: Deep learning and Transformers: a neuron by hand to backpropagation, tokens to attention, LLM concepts and prompting (part 2 of 2)

sentences.ar: يعني الـtoken الواحد تقريبا بيساوي 4 حروف أو 3 أرباع كلمة انجليزي
sentences.en: So one token is roughly 4 characters, or three quarters of an English word.

sentences.ar: وندخل على القسم الثالث حول Transformer وتحديداً الـattention mechanism ده بقى قلب التكنولوجيا كلها
sentences.en: We move on to part three: about the Transformer, specifically the attention mechanism, which is the heart of the whole technology.

sentences.ar: لو صممنا Transformer صغير جداً عشان نفهمه
sentences.en: Suppose we designed a very small Transformer so that we can understand it.

sentences.ar: الـd_model بتاعه 8 وعنده 2 heads والـd_head 4 وفيه block 1 بس
sentences.en: Its d_model is 8, it has 2 heads, d_head is 4, and it has 1 block only.

sentences.ar: الإجمالي كله 696 وزن
sentences.en: In total, 696 weights.

sentences.ar: الميزة هنا إننا نقدر نمشي وراء البيانات خطوة بخطوة ف14 مرحلة دقيقة
sentences.en: The advantage here is that we can follow the data step by step through 14 detailed stages.

sentences.ar: ونشوف الأرقام وهي بتنضرب في بعضها قدام عينينا
sentences.en: And we see the numbers being multiplied with each other right before our eyes.

sentences.ar: هنا بقى بتبدأ عملية الـ Attention
sentences.en: Here the Attention process begins.

sentences.ar: العملية دي بتعمل لنا شبكة أو Heat Map عرضها 8 مليانة درجات خام بتقول لنا مين مهتم بمين بالزبط
sentences.en: This process gives us a grid, or heat map, of width 8, full of raw scores telling us exactly who attends to whom.

sentences.ar: بس هنا فيه تركاية الموديل اللي بيتوقع الكلمة الجاية ماينفعش يبص على المستقبل صح؟
sentences.en: But here there is a catch: a model that predicts the next word cannot look at the future, right?

sentences.ar: الـmulti-head attention بيخلي كل head تركز على علاقة معينة بين الـtokens
sentences.en: Multi-head attention makes each head focus on a specific relationship between the tokens.

sentences.ar: القسم الرابع التنبؤ وتوليد الكلمات هنا هنشوف الموديل بيكتر ازاي
sentences.en: Part four: prediction and word generation; here we will see how the model works (one word is unclear in the audio).

sentences.ar: بنتحكم بقى في توزيع ده ازاي
sentences.en: So how do we control this distribution?

sentences.ar: عندنا الـtemperature لو خلناها من 0 ل 0 .3
sentences.en: We have the temperature: if we set it from 0 to 0.3...

sentences.ar: التوزيع بيبقى حاد ومحدد وده بيرفكت لتحليل البيانات
sentences.en: The distribution becomes sharp and specific, which is perfect for data analysis.

sentences.ar: بس لو رفعناها فوق 0 .7 التوزيع بيفرد ويبقى فيه إبداع وتنوع أكتر
sentences.en: But if we raise it above 0.7, the distribution spreads out and there is more creativity and diversity.

sentences.ar: القسم الخامس المفاهيم الأساسية للـLLMs أو النماذج اللغوية الضخمة
sentences.en: Part five: the core concepts of LLMs, or large language models.

sentences.ar: ولما بنكبر لـscale الـLLMs دي ما هي إلا نفس الـTransformer اللي شرحناه بس بحجم عملاق ومتضرب على داتا رهيبة
sentences.en: When we scale up, these LLMs are nothing but the same Transformer we explained, only at a giant size and run on huge data.

sentences.ar: في شوية مصطلحات لازم نعرفها
sentences.en: There are some terms we need to know.

sentences.ar: الـcontext window مثلا دي أقصى عدد tokens الموديل يشوفه في المرة وبتوصل من 4000 ل 128000
sentences.en: The context window, for example, is the maximum number of tokens the model can see at one time, and it ranges from 4000 to 128000.

sentences.ar: وفيه الـhallucination ودي بتحصل لما الموديل يقول كلام مقنع جدا بس غلط تماما
sentences.en: And there is hallucination, which happens when the model says very convincing but completely wrong things.

sentences.ar: وعشان كده بنحتاج نعمل grounding أو نربط المخرجات بمصادر حقيقية زي تقنية الـRAG
sentences.en: That is why we need grounding, or to tie the outputs to real sources, like the RAG technique.

sentences.ar: القسم السادس والأخير معنا الـprompting وتطبيقاته العملية
sentences.en: Part six and last with us: prompting and its practical applications.

sentences.ar: إزاي نوظف كل اللي فهمنا ده في الشغل كتابة الـprompt الصح مش مجرد دردشة مع الموديل
sentences.en: How we put everything we understood into practice at work: writing the right prompt, not just chatting with the model.

sentences.ar: إحنا لازم نديله أوليب منصمة زي ملخص يومي مثلا ونديله الـschema ونحددله role persona
sentences.en: We must give it a structured format (the word is unclear in the audio), like a daily summary, give it the schema, and assign it a role persona.

sentences.ar: يعني نطلب منه يكلمنا كمهندس أو كمدير
sentences.en: That means we ask it to talk to us as an engineer or as a manager.

sentences.ar: بنستخدم techniques زي zero-shot وfew-shot
sentences.en: We use techniques like zero-shot and few-shot.

sentences.ar: والأهم من كل ده لازم دايما نعمل validate للنتائج نستخرج الـSQL أو نعمل parse للـJSON عشان نتأكد إنه كله سليم
sentences.en: And most important of all, we must always validate the results: extract the SQL or parse the JSON to make sure it is all sound.

sentences.ar: تعالوا نشوف تطبيق عملي عندنا أداتين الـInsightsGenerator
sentences.en: Let's see a practical application: we have two tools, the InsightsGenerator.

sentences.ar: ده بياخد مقاييس يومية زي 156 طلب وإيراد 45890 وAOV 294
sentences.en: It takes daily metrics such as 156 orders, revenue 45890 and AOV 294.

sentences.ar: وبيطلع ملخص بلغة البزنس بـtemperature واطية جدا 0 .3 عشان ادق
sentences.en: And it produces a summary in business language, with a very low temperature of 0.3 to be more precise.

sentences.ar: الأداة التانية بقى هي الـAnomalyExplainer اللي بتحقق في الأرقام الغريبة
sentences.en: The second tool is the AnomalyExplainer, which investigates the strange numbers.

sentences.ar: الموديلز هنا بتعتمد على أدوات خارجية تجيب الداتا دي عشان متهلوسش
sentences.en: The models here rely on external tools that fetch this data so that they do not hallucinate.

sentences.ar: تخيلوا معي كان المتوقع يوم الحد إيرادات 50,000 بس الفعلي طلع 28,500 بس
sentences.en: Imagine with me: the expected revenue on Sunday was 50,000, but the actual came out at only 28,500.

sentences.ar: الموديل هنا دخل حل للداتا
sentences.en: The model here went into the data.

sentences.ar: وشرح لنا أن السبب كان timeouts في بوابة الدفع من الساعة 2 لـ4 العصر بسبب عاصفة ثلجية
sentences.en: And it explained to us that the cause was timeouts in the payment gateway from 2 to 4 in the afternoon, because of a snowstorm.

sentences.ar: الشرح ده كله طالع بناء على الداتا الحقيقية
sentences.en: All of this explanation comes out based on the real data.

sentences.ar: الجملة دي بقى هي الخلاصة لأي حد بتاع داتا
sentences.en: This sentence is the takeaway for anyone who works with data.

sentences.ar: الـ SQL بيعمل الحسابات والـ LLM مجرد بيشرح
sentences.en: SQL does the calculations, and the LLM just explains.

sentences.ar: الموديل مش آلة حسبة دقيقة الكود هو اللي بيحسب صح
sentences.en: The model is not an accurate calculator; the code is what computes correctly.

sentences.ar: دور الـ LLM إنه يصيغ ويلخص ويوضح لنا الأرقام دي بطريقة سلسة
sentences.en: The role of the LLM is to phrase, summarize and clarify these numbers for us in a smooth way.

sentences.ar: وبكده نكون وصلنا لنهاية الشرح مشينا الرحلة من أول ما حسبنا neuron بإيدينا
sentences.en: And with that we have reached the end of the explainer; we walked the journey from when we computed a neuron by hand.

sentences.ar: وشوفنا مشاكل learning rate لحد ما فككنا Transformer خطوة بخطوة ووصولاً للـ prompt templates
sentences.en: We saw the learning rate problems, took the transformer apart step by step, and ended up at the prompt templates.

sentences.ar: بعد ما كل الأرقام وتفاصيل دي بقت شفافة وواضحة قدامكم
sentences.en: After all these numbers and details have become transparent and clear in front of you.

sentences.ar: يا ترى ايه اللي ممكن تبنوه بالادوات دي
sentences.en: I wonder what you could build with these tools.

sentences.ar: الخيارات كلها مفتوحة للتجربة
sentences.en: All the options are open for experimentation.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.

glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

metaphors.metaphor: Text → token tiles → vectors rise; Q·K beams form attention weights; heatmap matrix; residual river; next-token probability bars (§6.17)

**Vector galaxy**: meaning as position; query probe; nearest neighbours ignite (cosine); a document **shatters into chunks**; top-k pulled from thousands; reranker conveyor; **context tunnel** with a limit, where middle chunks fade (lost in the middle); "retrieval is a query, not permission" access gate; agent loop inside **two guard rings**
metaphors.failure_fix: Hallucination = red corrupted branch → grounding with citations; vocabulary mismatch → hybrid search

metaphors.metaphor: Temperature/top-p as a dial sharpening or flattening the distribution

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
Pulse a target 1-4 times.
Text broken into tokens that stream past (optionally with ids).
Beams from a focus token to the tokens it attends to.
A token x token attention matrix (<= 16 tokens).
Bars (single or stacked) with token colours; values carry refs.
An embedding galaxy of seeded clusters (<= 1,500 points); a query probe finds nearest neighbours.
A target shatters into seeded blocks.
A context window as a tunnel; items enter and the oldest are evicted on overflow.
An agent loop (plan -> act -> observe) with guard checkpoints that can block a step.
Dials for sampling parameters (temperature, top-p ...).
Deep-Dive entry card with parent chapter and prerequisite concepts.
